extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, regulators, researchers, and advocates interested in the economic effects of federal regulation
extracted.subtask_description: A concise policy-analytic brief summarizing research on the cumulative economic and distributional costs of federal regulatory growth and recommending that policymakers account for system-wide accumulation when making regulatory decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify regulatory accumulation (use of RegData / restriction counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the total regulatory restrictions and changes over time (e.g., RegData finds total regulatory restrictions increased by nearly 20 percent since 1997 to more than 1 million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use text-analysis tools (such as RegData) or comparable metrics that count regulatory restrictions or 'words' of regulation to quantify accumulation and to track growth trends across years and industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess macroeconomic impact on GDP and growth rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate how cumulative regulations affect aggregate economic growth (examples: a 2013 study finds accumulation slowed growth by ~2% per year between 1949–2005; a 2016 endogenous growth model estimates a 0.8% annual reduction since 1980, implying a $4 trillion loss by 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply growth models (including endogenous growth frameworks) and counterfactual scenarios (e.g., regulatory burden held at earlier levels) to quantify long-run GDP and income effects of accumulated regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate distributional impacts across income groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine how regulatory costs are borne by different income groups; evidence shows accumulation disproportionately disadvantages unskilled workers and low-income households.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze regressivity by comparing regulatory costs as a share of income for low- vs high-income households (Mercatus finding: rules can cost six to eight times more as a share of income for low-income households).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure effect on consumer prices and price inflation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether increases in regulation volume are associated with higher consumer prices (one study estimates regulation-related price inflation as much as 10% for the 2000–2012 increase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate pass-through from regulatory compliance costs to retail prices and quantify how price increases affect households’ real purchasing power, especially for basic goods like food and utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze labor-market distortions and employment effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how added regulatory burden affects employment levels, shifts workers into compliance jobs, and causes permanent losses in lifetime earnings due to skill mismatches and reduced demand for production workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study sectoral employment changes, displacement effects, wage implications, and lifetime-earnings losses (evidence includes nearly three years of prior annual income lost for displaced workers in some estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess impact on inequality and poverty rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether higher regulatory burdens and entry requirements are associated with greater income inequality and higher poverty incidence (Mercatus studies link increased effective federal regulatory burden to rises in poverty and inequality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include state- or country-level cross-sectional/time-series analyses linking regulatory measures (e.g., procedures to start a business) to inequality and poverty outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate barriers to entry and effects on entrepreneurship
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether regulatory accumulation raises costs of market entry, deters startups, and disproportionately harms small firms relative to large incumbents (evidence: complication reduces number of small firms; small firms cope worse with regulatory growth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure number of procedures, fees, testing/education requirements, and regulatory complexity; compare firm entry rates, firm size distributions, and startup formation before/after regulatory changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider systemic interactions and cumulative effects (not just per-rule analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that even well-designed individual rules can create adverse effects via interactions with existing rules; accumulation produces duplicative, obsolete, conflicting, and contradictory rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move beyond isolated cost–benefit analysis of single rules to assessments of interactions, overlaps, and the overall regulatory stock; consider institutional reforms to detect and mitigate harmful accumulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure regulatory complexity/procedural burden (number of procedures to start a business)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify procedural requirements (e.g., steps to legally open a business) as an indicator of regulatory complication, which is associated with higher inequality and lower business formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use counts of procedures, licensing steps, fees, required tests/education, and administrative burdens as inputs when assessing economic and distributional consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for compounding effects over time on small businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider that regulatory accumulation has a compounding effect that increasingly burdens small businesses, reducing hiring and competitive entry over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model cumulative compliance costs and their growth-rate impacts on small-firm viability and hiring decisions versus large incumbents; include dynamic, multi-period analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh regulatory benefits against broader economy- and distribution-level costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Policymakers should more fully consider consequences of regulatory accumulation (economic growth loss, price effects, inequality, entrepreneurship suppression) before adding rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate system-level cost estimates and distributional analyses into regulatory decisionmaking; consider substantive reform or independent review mechanisms to limit harmful accumulation.
